title: Python Code Lab: Fix & Build
description: Debug broken Python code, complete missing functions, and solve coding puzzles! Each challenge tests a different programming concept -- from variables and loops to lists and functions. Write real Python code and see if your solution passes the test cases.
learning_objectives: Understand Python syntax, variables, and data types
Practice debugging code by identifying and fixing errors
Learn to write functions, loops, and conditional statements
Develop computational thinking and problem-solving skills
Understand how lists, strings, and basic data structures work

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each coding challenge carefully -- it describes what the code should do
Look at the provided code in the editor -- some code has bugs, some needs completing
Fix or complete the code so it produces the expected output
Click 'Run' to test your code against the test cases
Earn points for correct solutions -- bonus points for first-try success!
tips: Read the expected output carefully before editing the code
Check for common Python errors: indentation, missing colons, wrong variable names
Use print() statements to debug if you are stuck
Remember: Python uses 0-based indexing for lists and strings

challenges.title: Fix the Greeting
challenges.description: This function should return a greeting message like 'Hello, Priya!' but it has a bug. Fix it!
challenges.hint: Python is case-sensitive. Check the variable name carefully.

challenges.title: Sum of a List
challenges.description: Complete this function to return the sum of all numbers in a list. Do NOT use the built-in sum() function.
challenges.hint: Use the += operator to add each number to the running total.

challenges.title: Even or Odd Counter
challenges.description: This function should count how many even numbers are in a list. Fix the bug!
challenges.hint: A number is even when divided by 2 the remainder is 0, not 1.

challenges.title: Reverse a String
challenges.description: Complete this function to reverse a string. For example, 'India' should become 'aidnI'.
challenges.hint: Python slicing with a step of -1 reverses a string: text[::-1]

challenges.title: FizzBuzz Classic
challenges.description: Complete the FizzBuzz function: return 'Fizz' if n is divisible by 3, 'Buzz' if divisible by 5, 'FizzBuzz' if divisible by both, otherwise return the number as a string.
challenges.hint: Check for FizzBuzz first (both 3 and 5), then Fizz (3), then Buzz (5), else the number.

challenges.title: Find the Maximum
challenges.description: Write a function that finds the largest number in a list WITHOUT using the built-in max() function.
challenges.hint: Start with the first element as the biggest, then loop through comparing each number.

challenges.title: Palindrome Checker
challenges.description: Complete this function to check if a word is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards). Ignore case. 'Madam' should return True.
challenges.hint: Convert to lowercase first with .lower(), then compare the string with its reverse.

challenges.title: Cricket Average Calculator
challenges.description: Virat's scores in 5 innings are given as a list. Complete the function to calculate his batting average, rounded to 1 decimal place. The average should exclude innings where he scored 0 (did not bat).
challenges.initial_code:
def batting_average(scores):
    # Filter out 0 scores, then calculate average
    valid = [s for s in scores if s > 0]
    if len(valid) == 0:
        return 0.0
    # Calculate and return average rounded to 1 decimal
    pass
challenges.hint: Use sum(valid) / len(valid) and round() to 1 decimal place.

challenges.title: Password Strength Checker
challenges.description: Write a function that checks password strength. Return 'Strong' if the password has: length >= 8, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, and one digit. Otherwise return 'Weak'.
challenges.hint: Use .isupper(), .islower(), .isdigit() with any() to check character types.

challenges.title: Fibonacci Sequence
challenges.description: Complete the function to return the first n numbers of the Fibonacci sequence. Fibonacci: each number is the sum of the two before it. fib(6) = [0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5]
challenges.hint: In a loop from 2 to n, each new number = seq[-1] + seq[-2] (last two elements).

transfer_exercises.real_world: Making fast calls during a team project deadline crunch
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice making a decision in under 60 seconds on something you've been procrastinating. Reflect on the outcome.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from mistakes in rapid gameplay
transfer_exercises.real_world: Bouncing back after a failed presentation or test
transfer_exercises.challenge: Write down one recent failure and three specific things you learned from it.

glossary_terms.definition: The mental effort required to process information and make decisions.
glossary_terms.example: Having too many options at once makes decisions harder and slower.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Working memory has limits. Experts chunk information into patterns, reducing cognitive load and enabling faster decisions.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Experienced doctors diagnose faster not because they think harder, but because they recognize patterns instantly.

glossary_terms.definition: Identifying recurring structures or relationships in information.
glossary_terms.example: Noticing that certain question types always have two plausible answers helps you focus faster.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Pattern recognition is a core skill in chess, medicine, engineering, and sport. It develops through deliberate practice.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Air traffic controllers recognize dangerous flight patterns faster than computers because of years of pattern training.

glossary_terms.definition: The ability to direct mental attention toward what matters most and ignore distractions.
glossary_terms.example: Under time pressure, completing questions you're confident about before tackling harder ones.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Focus is a trainable skill. The Pomodoro method, mindfulness, and deliberate practice all improve sustained attention.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Olympic athletes train mental focus as rigorously as physical skills — pressure performance depends on it.

coaching_moment: Notice how each decision here requires weighing multiple options. Strategic thinkers pause before choosing — what's the long-term implication of each answer?
cultural_context: Scientific literacy is a strategic priority under NEP 2020, which emphasises inquiry-based learning over rote memorisation. Python Code Lab: Fix & Build builds the analytical instincts that support strong performance in India's science curricula.
reflection_prompt: What pattern did you start to recognize as you played? How will you use it next time?
